newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai jewellery turnover higher on Ramadan.
newsitem.headline: Dubai jewellery turnover higher on Ramadan.

text.p: Jewellery sales from the Gulf Arab trading post of Dubai to Saudi Arabia have risen ahead of the Islamic holy month of Ramadan, Dubai-based traders said on Sunday.

But bullion sales to the main Indian subcontinent markets remained uninspired despite three-year price lows, Indian wedding demand, strong imports into Dubai and a relaxation of rules governing the import of gold into India, they said.
"Jewellery sales for Saudi Arabia are growing because of Ramadan," said a Dubai- based supplier to the Saudi market.
Saudi Arabia is the Gulf's biggest consumer of gold -- predominately in the form of gold jewellery such as bangles and finished pieces -- counting for 193 tonnes in 1995.
The end of fasting during Ramadan is celebrated by Eid al-Fitr which often involves jewellery purchases as presents.
The major Gulf gold souks of Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates typically see an upturn in their retail business.

Indian wedding demand continued to stoke Dubai bullion turnover but with the season set to end by the end of next month some traders questioned how much more bullion the India market could take from Dubai.
"Business has not been as good as I had hoped...Buying is not as strong as last year," said one Dubai-based trader said.

But other traders took encouragement from new Indian law that allows Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to import 10 kg (22 lbs) of gold every six months at a customs rate of 220 Indian rupees ($6.13) per 10 grams (0.35 oz).
NRIs were previously allowed to import only five kg.
"It should attract more (bullion) carriers (to India)," one wholesaler said.

India -- the world's largest consumer of the yellow metal -- is the main re- export market for Dubai, which imported over 318 tonnes of bullion between January and November last year, mainly from Switzerland and Britain.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 4,998 UAE dirhams ($1,361), down 107 dirhams from December 30.
Ten gram pieces were assessed at 427 dirhams.
International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $361.40-$361.90, hovering close to three-year lows.
